groups.text: Nannan’s father runs an enterprise near the Ming Tombs selling batteries and drills to the Daqing Oilfield. Hoping to get the qualification to help govern it, Nannan made much preparation and then left her motherland with her visa to study in America. Having reached her destination, she settled in an inn recommended by the travel agent.
groups.zh: 楠楠的父亲在明十三陵附近经营一家企业，向大庆油田销售电池和钻机。希望获得资格，将来帮助管理企业，楠楠做了大量准备，然后带着签证离开祖国，到美国留学。到达目的地后，她住进了旅行社推荐的一家小旅馆。

groups.text: As far as Nannan was concerned, she always kept it up in China. But she had to acknowledge it was not easy to adjust herself to the new academic requirements, which were not in line with those in China. Though she was occupied with lectures and seminars day in and day out, the essays she drafted were still criticised by her tutors.
groups.zh: 就楠楠而言，她在中国时一直保持着良好的表现。但她不得不承认，要适应新的学业要求并不容易，这些要求与中国的不一样。尽管她日复一日地忙于听课和参加研讨会，她起草的论文还是会受到导师的批评。

groups.text: As for her routine life, she felt that it was hard to fit in, too. For example, she found English idioms difficult to understand. And it was out of the question to eat delicious Chinese foods though many optional cafeterias served abundant substitutes.
groups.zh: 至于日常生活，她觉得很难融入，也是如此（too 表示“也”）。比如，她发现英语习语很难理解。而吃到美味的中餐，更是不可能，尽管有许多自助餐厅可选，提供丰富的替代食物。

groups.text: In addition, she had to wait in a queue early for the minibus that took her to school and it was usually so cold that she felt numb. What bothered her most was that she received no apology when her sleeping was disturbed by a barking dog in a shopkeeper’s cage. Luckily, with her parents comforting her by videophone, she became autonomous soon and eventually got her bachelor’s degree successfully.
groups.zh: 此外，她还得早早排队等候，等送她去学校的小巴，而当时通常非常冷，冷得她都麻木了。最困扰她的是，她没有得到任何道歉，当她的睡眠受到干扰时，干扰来自店主笼子里一只不停叫的狗。幸运的是，父母通过视频电话安慰她，她很快变得独立，最终顺利获得了学士学位。
